subject.title: fix(browser): keep CDP cursor text previews UTF-16 safe

question: Should OpenClaw accept page-side surrogate scrubbing as worthwhile CDP transport hardening even though the current final cursor preview is already safe?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically reasonable, but the supplied evidence establishes only a cleaner intermediate wire value rather than an observable final-output failure, so merge value depends on owner judgment.

options.title: Reframe and test the full pipeline
options.body: Treat this as transport hardening, retain one canonical branch, and add a regression proving equivalence and safety through the actual page-101 plus Node-100 path.

options.title: Require an observable failure
options.body: Keep both branches unmergeable until a current-main cursor snapshot, CDP consumer, or downstream operation demonstrably fails because of the intermediate surrogate.

options.title: Accept the hardening as submitted
options.body: Land this branch based on the narrower invariant that malformed surrogate units should not cross the CDP return-by-value boundary.

recommendation.title: Reframe and test the full pipeline
recommendation.body: Treat this as transport hardening, retain one canonical branch, and add a regression proving equivalence and safety through the actual page-101 plus Node-100 path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent Chrome/CDP diagnostics work makes this the best available owner for deciding whether the transport invariant merits code.
